reader.decision: Hold approval for now. I accept the direction of the lock fix (900s TTL, no `none` backend), but I won't approve it until we confirm that us-east can reach `redis-locks`. I am not choosing idempotent purchase orders instead, because that change is in code nobody has read.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the fix depends on `redis-locks` being reachable from us-east, and it found no file that settles this. If us-east can't reach Redis, removing `none` could break the job there. The idempotent alternative touches `stockpile.purchasing`, which was not read, so I can't rule on it either.

reconstruction.problem: `restock-planner` sent two purchase orders for HT-4410 because the `reorder` lock didn't keep the second pod out. In eu-west (redis backend) the 60s TTL expired during a job that takes about 4 minutes, so pod B got the lock at 01:02. In us-east (`lock_backend: none`) `acquire` always returns True, so there was no lock at all. Which region produced the real duplicate is unknown.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Halvorsen Tools receives two identical purchase orders. In us-east nothing marks the job as running. In eu-west the lock lapses before the job ends.
reconstruction.fix: Change `ttl_seconds` from 60 to 900 in `planner/reorder.py`. Delete the `backend == "none"` branch in `planner/locks.py` and keep the `backend` argument. Set `lock_backend: redis` in `config/us-east.yaml`. The alternative is an idempotency key (SKU, supplier, run date) in `create_purchase_order`.
reconstruction.cost: A crashed pod holds the lock for up to 15 minutes, which the message calls harmless for a nightly job. The risk is that us-east may not be able to reach `redis-locks`, and that is unverified. The idempotent option needs a change in `stockpile.purchasing`, which is outside this repo and unread.

follow_up_questions: Can us-east pods reach the `redis-locks` Redis? Check network policy, deployed config, or a connectivity test from a us-east pod.

What does `locks.acquire` do if Redis is unreachable: fail open (run without a lock), fail closed (skip the job), or raise an error? This decides whether the fix could silently stop the nightly job in us-east.
Does the job need to run in both regions, or should one lock cover both? The message only describes a per-region lock, and a shared lock may be needed if both regions order the same SKU.
reader.closing_answer: Neither yet. I lean toward the 900s TTL plus removing `none`, but only after someone confirms that us-east can reach `redis-locks` and what `acquire` does when Redis is down. I'd pursue idempotent purchase orders as a follow-up, once someone has read `stockpile.purchasing`, so the fix doesn't depend only on Redis.
